info.title: Wherobots Cloud API
info.description:
Wherobots Cloud API OpenAPI specification.

    These are the API docs for the Wherobots API. You can use this to test out the API and see what it does.
    The underlying OPENAPI spec can be found at /openapi.json. This can be used to generate clients for the API.

    The Authorize button below will allow you to input an access token to authenticate to our API.
    Then all of the requests on the page should work.

post.summary: Exchange token for Iceberg REST access
post.description:
Exchange credentials for Open Source (OSS) Iceberg REST Client (IRC).

OSS IRC (< 1.10.x) uses 2 grant types:
- token-exchange: Defined by the OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange spec (RFC 8693).
  Exchange a valid, unexpired (OAuth) access token for a new access token with the same or smaller scopes.
- client_credentials: Defined by the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework spec (RFC 6749).
  Exchange a client credential (i.e. Wherobots API Key) for an access token.

Use cases:
1. [client_credentials] Users who has an API key yet no OAuth JWT token.
Request format:
    {
        "grant_type": "client_credentials",
        "client_id": "<customer_id>", (Wherobots Customer Ext ID)
        "client_secret": "<api_key>", (Wherobots API Key)
        "scope": "<requested_scope>" ("catalog" for now, to be extended in the future)
    }
2. [token-exchange] Users who already has an valid, unexpired OAuth JWT token.
Request format:
    {
        "grant_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange", (OSS IRC always use this exact string)
        "scope": "<requested_scope>",
        "subject_token": "<current_unexpired_access_token>",
        "subject_token_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token", (OSS IRC always use this exact string)
        "actor_token": "<optional_actor_token>", (not used currently)
        "actor_token_type": "<actor_token_type>" (not used currently)
    }
Note: the optional actor_token is used for permission delegation, which is NOT
currently supported, and thus has no effect even if provided. The "subject_token_type"
has to be "access_token" at the moment - we currently only support exchanging access tokens.

Return temporary AWS credentials scoped to the requested S3 path.

Resolution order:
1. Managed storage (org file store bucket)
2. WherobotsDB releases bucket (if the org has the feature)
3. User-defined storage integrations (prefix match)

`payload.access_mode` controls whether returned credentials are read-only
or include write permissions.

Returns empty credentials for public buckets (no role_arn).

200.description: Temporary credentials scoped to the requested path with read or read/write access

404.description: No storage source matches the requested path

post.description:
Initiates the upgrade process for the organization's subscription with
Stripe-based payments.

This creates a new Stripe SetupIntent and a PENDING StripeSubscription to
initiate the upgrade flow. The client will use the returned intent secret to
complete the payment method setup on the frontend. The PENDING StripeSubscription
does not become the organization's active subscription as a result of this call
(see the upgrade_confirmation endpoint below).

The Stripe subscription webhook handler will then finalize the upgrade once the payment method is
confirmed and successfully attached by Stripe (see src.routers.webhook.stripe).

Confirms the subscription upgrade process for the organization's Stripe-based subscription.

Called by the frontend after the Stripe SetupIntent process is completed, as notification to the
backend that the pending StripeSubscription can now be considered the active subscription for the organization.

This is a UX optimization so that the user will see the pending state immediately after completing the SetupIntent,
instead of having to wait for the Stripe webhook to be processed. The upgrade will still be finalized properly by
the webhook handler even if the call to this endpoint fails or is never made.

Cancels the organization's Stripe subscription.

This will cancel the subscription in Orb (stopping billing), downgrade the
organization to the Community plan, and mark the subscription as stopped.

post.description:
Handle a WorkOS AuthKit User Registration Action.

WorkOS POSTs a signed payload at sign-up time; we verify the signature, then
return a *signed* Allow/Deny verdict. Signature verification always runs and
always fails closed (bad signature -> 401, missing secret -> 500) regardless
of environment. The domain restriction itself is only enforced when the
running environment is in ``signup_restricted_environments`` and an allowlist
is configured; otherwise the action is a pass-through (always Allow).

KubeAppCreationMeta.title: KubeAppCreationMeta
KubeAppCreationMeta.description:
``event_meta`` shape for ``EventCode.APP_START_CREATION``.

Captures decisions pinned at kube_app creation time so cancel/destroy can
consult them later without re-deriving. Currently only carries the v2
dispatcher marker — set to ``True`` when the LaunchDarkly flag routes the
kube_app through the unified ``KubeAppWorkflow`` (ENGP-336 Stream E).
Legacy creates leave ``event_meta`` ``None`` so this model isn't even
constructed; cleanup at v2 100% rollout deletes this class.

NodeSchedulingMeta.title: NodeSchedulingMeta
NodeSchedulingMeta.description:
Metadata captured at node-scheduling time.

``node_preexisted`` is True when the pod landed on a node that existed
before the pod was created, False when the node was provisioned for
the pod (cold start).

Operation.title: Operation
Operation.description:
Describes the operation.

Possible operation values are:
    - append: Only data files were added and no files were removed.
    - replace: Data and delete files were added and removed without changing table data;
        i.e., compaction, changing the data file format, or relocating data files.
    - overwrite: Data and delete files were added and removed in a logical overwrite operation.
    - delete: Data files were removed and their contents logically deleted and/or delete files
        were added to delete rows.

WorkloadCostAvailable.title: WorkloadCostAvailable
WorkloadCostAvailable.description: A workload cost we were able to resolve.

WorkloadCostStatus.title: WorkloadCostStatus
WorkloadCostStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a materialized workload cost record.

LIVE     - Workload is still running; cost may continue to accumulate.
           Refreshed from the upstream billing system on read if older
           than the settling window.
SETTLING - Workload finished recently; cost is approaching its final
           value but the upstream may still emit late events. Continues
           to be refreshed until the settling window elapses.
FINAL    - Cost is sealed. No further refreshes; FINAL never reverts
           to LIVE or SETTLING regardless of update_time ordering.

WorkloadCostUnavailable.title: WorkloadCostUnavailable
WorkloadCostUnavailable.description: A workload cost we could not resolve, with a structured reason.

WorkloadCostUnavailableReason.title: WorkloadCostUnavailableReason
WorkloadCostUnavailableReason.description:
Why a workload cost could not be returned.

NOT_FOUND           - The kube_app_id is not known to the billing system,
                      or the caller is not authorized to see it.
                      Indistinguishable by design (avoids leaking the
                      existence of unrelated workloads).
UPSTREAM_ERROR      - The upstream billing system failed or timed out and
                      we have no cached value to serve. Caller may retry.
UPSTREAM_RATE_LIMIT - The upstream billing system signaled a rate limit;
                      caller should back off.

WorkloadCostsOutput.title: WorkloadCostsOutput
WorkloadCostsOutput.description:
Batch response envelope.

Contract (enforced by the service that constructs this, not by the
schema): `costs.keys() == set(input.kube_app_ids)`. Every requested
id appears in the response exactly once, either as Available or
Unavailable. The service layer is responsible for upholding this;
the wire shape is intentionally permissive so it doesn't add runtime
cost on every serialization.
